nodes.name: Internal model principle for linear output synchronization
nodes.statement: In \cite{WielandAU2011}, it is shown that the internal model principle is the sufficient and necessary condition for non-trivial linear output synchronization.
conclusions: the internal model principle is the sufficient and necessary condition for non-trivial linear output synchronization

nodes.name: Multi-agent system of N agents
nodes.statement: Consider a multi-agent system consisting of $N$ agents.

nodes.name: Nonlinear affine agent dynamics
nodes.statement: Each agent has the following dynamics modeled by \begin{equation} \left\{\begin{split} \dot{x}_i &= f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)u_i \\ y_i & = h_i(x_i), \end{split}\right., \quad i=1,2,\cdots,N, \end{equation} where $x_i$ is the state, defined on a neighborhood $X_i$ of the origin of $\mathbb{R}^{n_i}$, $u_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i}$ is the input, and $y_i\in\mathbb{R}^p$ is the output.
nodes.statement_short: Agent $i$: $\dot x_i=f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)u_i$, $y_i=h_i(x_i)$, with state on a neighborhood $X_i$ of the origin.

nodes.name: Smoothness of agent vector fields
nodes.statement: The vector $f_i(x_i)$ and the $m_i$ columns of matrix $g_i(x_i)$ are smooth (i.e., $C^{\infty}$) vector fields on $X_i$.

nodes.name: Smoothness of output map
nodes.statement: $h_i(x_i)$ is a smooth mapping defined on $X_i$.

nodes.name: Output tracking of a common exosystem
nodes.statement: Each agent drives its output to track the output of a common exosystem, as formulated by \begin{subequations} \begin{align} &\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)\\ &y_i+q(w_0)\rightarrow 0. \end{align} \end{subequations}

nodes.name: Exosystem
nodes.statement: The first equation describes an autonomous system, the so-called exosystem, defined in a neighborhood $W_0$ of the origin of $\mathbb{R}^s$.
differentia: defined in a neighborhood $W_0$ of the origin of $\mathbb{R}^s$

nodes.name: Smoothness of exosystem
nodes.statement: The vector $s(w_0)$ is a smooth vector field on $W_0$ and $q(w_0)$ is a smooth map defined on $W_0$.

nodes.name: Synchronized output regulation (SOR)
nodes.statement: As for the SOR, the requirements on output $y_i$ are two folds: one is that $y_i$ belongs to a fixed family of trajectories determined by the pair of $(s(w_0), q(w_0))$ with the corresponding initial condition $w_0(0)$ being allowed to vary on a predefined set $\hat{W}_0\subset W_0$; the other is that $y_i\rightarrow y_j$ for all $i,j\in\mathcal{V}$.
nodes.statement_short: SOR requires each output to lie in the exosystem-generated trajectory family and all outputs to synchronize.

nodes.name: Communication digraph
nodes.statement: Generally, a digraph $\mathcal{G}=\{\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E}\}$ is used to depict the communication channels of multi-agent system \eqref{II01}, where node set $\mathcal{V}=\{1,2,\cdots,N\}$ is the index set of agents and edge set $\mathcal{E}\subseteq \{\mathcal{V}\times \mathcal{V}\}$ consists of ordered pair of nodes $(i,j)$, called edge.

nodes.name: Parent node and child node
nodes.statement: An edge $(i,j)\in\mathcal{E}$ if and only if there is communication channel from node $i$ to node $j$, where node $i$ is called parent node and node $j$ is called child node.

nodes.name: Directed path
nodes.statement: A directed path of digraph is a sequence of edges with form $(i_1,i_2), (i_2,i_3), \cdots$.

nodes.name: Tree (root node)
nodes.statement: A tree $\mathcal{G}_t=\{\mathcal{V}_t,\mathcal{E}_t\}$ is a graph where every node has exactly one parent node except for one node, the so-called root node, which has no parent node but has a directed path to every other node.
differentia: every node has exactly one parent node except for one node, the so-called root node, which has no parent node but has a directed path to every other node

nodes.name: Subgraph
nodes.statement: The graph $\mathcal{G}_s=\{\mathcal{V}_s,\mathcal{E}_s\}$ is a subgraph of $\mathcal{G}$ if $\mathcal{V}_s\subseteq\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{E}_s\subseteq \mathcal{E}\bigcap(\mathcal{V}_s\times \mathcal{V}_s)$.

nodes.name: Spanning tree
nodes.statement: The tree $\mathcal{G}_t$ is a spanning tree of graph $\mathcal{G}$ if $\mathcal{G}_t$ is a subgraph of $\mathcal{G}$ with $\mathcal{V}_t=\mathcal{V}$.

nodes.name: Switching graph
nodes.statement: A switching graph, defined on a piecewise constant switching signal $\sigma(t):\mathbb{R}^+\mapsto \mathcal{P}=\{1,2,\cdots,P\}$, is denoted by $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}=\{\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E}_{\sigma(t)}\}$, where set $\mathcal{P}$ indexes the total $P$ number digraphs and $\mathcal{E}_{s}\subseteq\mathcal{V}\times \mathcal{V}$ with $s\in\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.name: Switching instants
nodes.statement: The time instants when $\sigma$ switches is denoted by an increasing sequence $t_k$, $k=0,1,2,\cdots,$ with $t_0=0$.

nodes.name: Active graph index
nodes.statement: Denote by $\sigma_k$ the value of $\sigma(t)$ when $t\in[t_{k-1},t_k)$.

nodes.name: Adjacency and Laplacian matrices
nodes.statement: Denote by $\mathcal{A}^{\sigma_k}$ and $L^{\sigma_k}$ the adjacency matrix and the Laplacian matrix of $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma_k}$, respectively.

nodes.name: Dwell-time assumption
nodes.statement: We assume that any two consecutive switching instants are separated by a dwell-time $D_t$, i.e., $t_k-t_{k-1}\ge D_t$ so as to guarantee that the switching graph is non-chattering and zeno behavior cannot occur.

nodes.name: Union graph
nodes.statement: A union graph $\mathcal{G}_{[t^1,t^2]}$ over an interval time $[t^1, t^2]$ is defined by $\mathcal{G}_{[t^1,t^2]}\triangleq (\mathcal{V}, \bigcup_{t\in[t^1,t^2]}\mathcal{E}_{\sigma(t)})$ that corresponds to a graph consisting of all nodes in $\mathcal{V}$ and all edges that appear at any time $t\in[t^1,t^2]$.

nodes.name: Coupled exosystem
nodes.statement: In the first step, each agent builds the following coupled exosystem, based on the communication graph $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}$, \begin{equation} \dot{w}_i = s(w_i)+\sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i), \end{equation} where $a_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}$ denotes the $i$th row and $j$th column element of adjacency matrix $\mathcal{A}^{\sigma(t)}$ of graph $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}$. If $(j,i)\in\mathcal{E}_{\sigma(t)}$, then $a^{\sigma(t)}_{ij}>0$; otherwise, $a^{\sigma(t)}_{ij}=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Each agent runs a local copy of the exosystem, diffusively coupled to neighbors' copies over the switching graph.

nodes.name: Tracking error
nodes.statement: In this case, the tracking error for each agent is defined as \begin{equation} e_i = h_i(x_i)+q(w_i). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Distributed dynamic state feedback controller
nodes.statement: \textbf{Distributed dynamic state feedback controller} \begin{equation} \left\{ \begin{split} & \dot{w}_i = s(w_i)+\sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i),\\ & u_i = \alpha_i(x_i,w_i) \end{split} \right., \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} where $\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)$ is a $C^k$ (for some integer $k\ge2$) mapping defined on $X_i\times W$, satisfying $a_i(0,0)=0$.

nodes.name: State feedback closed-loop system
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{II04} and \eqref{II01} yields the following closed-loop system, \begin{equation} \left\{\begin{split} \dot{x}_i& = f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(x_i,w_i) \\ \dot{w}_i& = s(w_i)+\sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i) \end{split}, \right.\quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} which has an equilibrium at, $(x_i,w_i)=(0,0)$ for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$.

nodes.name: Distributed dynamic output feedback controller
nodes.statement: \textbf{Distributed dynamic output feedback controller} \begin{equation} \left\{ \begin{split} \dot{w}_i& = s(w_i)+\sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i)\\ \dot{z}_i& = \eta_i(z_i,y_i)\\ u_i &= \alpha_i(z_i,w_i) \end{split}, \right. \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} where $z_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}$ is the observer state, defined on a neighborhood $Z_i$ of the origin of $\mathbb{R}^{n_i}$. For each $y_i\in\mathbb{R}^p$, $\eta_i(z_i,y_i)$ is a $C^k$ vector field on $Z_i$ (for some integer $k\ge 2$).

nodes.name: Output feedback closed-loop system
nodes.statement: The closed-loop system under controller \eqref{II06} has the form \begin{equation} \left\{ \begin{split} \dot{x}_i&=f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(z_i,w_i)\\ \dot{z}_i & = \eta_i(z_i,h_i(x_i))\\ \dot{w}_i & = s(w_i) + \sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i) \end{split}, \right.\quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} which has an equilibrium, $(x_i,z_i,w_i)=(0,0,0)$ for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$, when $\eta_i(0,0)=0$ for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$.

nodes.name: Stacked vectors
nodes.statement: Define the stacked vector $x=[x_1^T,\cdots,x_N^T]^T$, $w=[w_1^T,\cdots,w_N^T]^T$ and $z=[z_1^T,\cdots,z_N^T]^T$.

nodes.name: Stacked domains
nodes.statement: Correspondingly, their domains are defined as $X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_N$, $W=W_1\times\cdots\times W_N$, and $Z=Z_1\times\cdots\times Z_N$.

nodes.name: State Feedback Synchronized Regulator Problem
nodes.statement: Find, if possible, $\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)$ for node $i$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item [1a)] the equilibrium $x=0$ of \begin{equation} \dot{x}_i = f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(x_i,0), \quad i\in\mathcal{V} \end{equation} is exponentially stable. \item [1b)] there are a neighborhood $U\subset X\times W$ of $(0,0)$ and a exosystem, \begin{equation} \dot{w}_0=s(w_0), \end{equation} defined on the neighborhood $W_0$ of origin of $\mathbb{R}^{s}$, such that, for each initial condition $(x(0),w(0))\in U$, there exists a initial condition $w_0(0)\in W_0$ for system \eqref{II09} such that the solution of \eqref{II05} satisfies \begin{equation} \lim_{t\rightarrow \infty} (h_i(x_i(t))+q(w_0(t))) = 0, \quad \forall\, i\in\mathcal{V}. \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Find local state feedback $\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)$ making the unforced closed loop exponentially stable and all outputs track a common exosystem.

nodes.name: Error feedback Synchronized Regulator Problem
nodes.statement: Find, if possible, $\alpha_i(z_i,w_i)$ and $\eta_i(z_i,y_i)$, such that \begin{itemize} \item [2a)] the equilibrium $(x,z)=0$ of \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\dot{x}_i=f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(z_i,0),\\ & \dot{z}_i=\eta_i(z_i,h_i(x_i)), \end{split}\quad \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} is exponentially stable. \item [2b)] there exists a neighborhood $U\subset X\times Z\times W$ of $(0,0,0)$ and an exosystem \begin{equation} \dot{w}_0=s(w_0) \end{equation} defined on a neighborhood $W_0$ of origin of $\mathbb{R}^{s}$, such that, for each initial condition $(x(0), z(0)$, $ w(0))\in U$, there exists a initial condition $w_0(0)\in W_0$ for system \eqref{II12} such that the solution of \eqref{II07} satisfies \begin{equation} \lim_{t\rightarrow \infty} (h_i(x_i(t))+q(w_0(t)))=0, \quad \forall\, i\in\mathcal{V}. \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Find dynamic output feedback $(\alpha_i,\eta_i)$ giving exponential stability and asymptotic tracking of a common exosystem output by all agents.

nodes.name: A1) Poisson stable exosystem
nodes.statement: The exosystem modeled by $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ has a stable equilibrium at $w_0=0$, and there is an open neighborhood of $w_0=0$ in which every point is Poisson stable.

nodes.name: A2) Stabilizable linear approximation
nodes.statement: The pair $\big(f_i(x_i),g_i(x_i)\big)$ has a stabilizable linear approximation at $x_i=0$, for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$.

nodes.name: A3) Detectable linear approximation
nodes.statement: The pair $\big(f_i(x_i),h_i(x_i)\big)$ has a detectable linear approximation at $x_i=0$ for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$.

nodes.name: A4) Bounded interconnectivity times condition
nodes.statement: There is a bounded time length $T$ and a starting time $t>0$ such that for each $k$, $k=1,2,\cdots$, the union graph $\mathcal{G}_{[t+(k-1)T,t+kT]}$ has a spanning tree embedded.

nodes.name: Local exponential synchronizability of coupled systems under switching graph
nodes.statement: Given a multi-agent system \eqref{II02} with communication graph $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}$satisfying assumption A4). If the largest Lyapunov exponent $\nu_{max}$ of system $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ and the consensus convergence rate $\alpha^*(T,t)$ of $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}$ are such that \begin{equation} \nu_{max}+\ln(\alpha^*(T,t))/T<0 \end{equation} then system \eqref{II02} is locally exponentially synchronizable.
assumptions: a multi-agent system \eqref{II02} with communication graph $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}$satisfying assumption A4)
the largest Lyapunov exponent $\nu_{max}$ of system $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ and the consensus convergence rate $\alpha^*(T,t)$ of $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}$ are such that
nodes.statement_short: If $\nu_{max}+\ln\alpha^*(T,t)/T<0$ under A4), the coupled exosystems locally exponentially synchronize.
nodes.label: le01

nodes.name: Flow of the exosystem vector field
nodes.statement: Denote by $\Phi_t^s(w^0)$ the flow of vector field $s(w_0)$, defined for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, with $w_0(0)=w^0$.

nodes.name: Maximum Lyapunov exponent
nodes.statement: Then the maximum Lyapunov exponent of dynamic system $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ is defined as \cite{CenciniBOOK2010} \begin{equation} \nu_{max} = \lim_{t\rightarrow \infty} \lim_{\delta w^0\rightarrow 0}\frac{1}{t} \ln\frac{\|\Phi_t^s(w^0+\delta w^0)-\Phi_t^s(w^0)\|}{\|\delta w^0\|} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Switching interval sequence
nodes.statement: Define the time interval sequence $\{\delta_k\}$ by $\delta_k = t_k-t_{k-1}$, $k=1,2,\cdots$.

nodes.name: Time instants $t^1$, $t^2$
nodes.statement: Let $t^1$ and $t^2$ be two time instants located in the time slots of $[t_{i-1}, t_i)$ and $[t_{j-1},t_j)$ with $i\le j$, respectively.

nodes.name: Consensus convergence rate
nodes.statement: Given a switching graph $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}$ satisfying Assumption A4) with given $t$ and $T$, its consensus convergent rate is defined as the supremum of the contract rate of transition matrix $\Phi(t+(k-1)T,t+kT)$ \cite{XiangIJC2011}, \begin{equation} \alpha^*(T,t)=\sup_k \alpha(\Phi(t+(k-1)T,t+kT)) \end{equation} where the contract rate $\alpha(\Phi)$ is defined as $\alpha(\Phi) = \max\limits_{x\neq 0, x\bot \mathbf{b}}\frac{\|\Phi^Tx\|}{\|x\|}$, and the transition matrix is defined as \begin{equation} \Phi(t^2,t^1)=e^{-L^{\sigma_j}(t^2-t_{j-1})}e^{-L^{\sigma_{j-1}}\delta_{j-1}}\cdots e^{-L^{\sigma_{i+1}}\delta_{i+1}}e^{-L^{\sigma_{i}}(t_i-t^1)} \end{equation} where $L^{\sigma_k}$ is the Laplacian matrix of graph $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma_k}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\alpha^*(T,t)$ is the supremum over windows of the contraction rate (orthogonal to $\mathbf{b}$) of the product of Laplacian exponentials.

nodes.name: All-ones vector
nodes.statement: Throughout of this paper, $\mathbf{b}$ denotes the vector with all elements being $1$.

nodes.name: Exponential synchronization of coupled exosystems
nodes.statement: Given a coupled exosystem \eqref{II02} with assumptions A1) and A4), then there is a dynamic system $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ such that for all initial conditions $w(0)\in\mathcal{\bar{W}}\subset W$, there is a initial condition $w_0(0)\in W_0$ such that the error $\delta w_i=w_i-w_0$ exponentially converges to zero, for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$.
assumptions: a coupled exosystem \eqref{II02} with assumptions A1) and A4)
conclusions: there is a dynamic system $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ such that for all initial conditions $w(0)\in\mathcal{\bar{W}}\subset W$, there is a initial condition $w_0(0)\in W_0$ such that the error $\delta w_i=w_i-w_0$  exponentially converges to zero, for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$
nodes.statement_short: Under A1) and A4), all local exosystem states converge exponentially to a common exosystem trajectory.
nodes.label: le02

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: According to Assumption A4) and definition \eqref{III03}, it follows that transition matrix $\Phi(t+(k-1)T,t+kT)$ is stochastic, indecomposable and aperiodic, and has exactly one trivial eigenvalue $1$ associated with eigenvector $\mathbf{b}$. Therefore, $\alpha^*(T,t)<1$. On the other hand, with assumption A1), $\nu_{max}\le 0$. If not, for any given $\epsilon$, there is a time $T_\epsilon$, such that for any $0<\|\delta w^0\|<\epsilon$, $\|\Phi_t^s(w^0+\delta w^0)\|>\epsilon$ for all $t>T_\epsilon$. This is contradictory to the feature of Poisson stable \cite{IsidoriTAC1990}. With $\nu_{max}\le0$ and $\alpha^*(T,t)<1$, making use of Lemma \ref{le01} yields that there is a neighborhood $\bar{W}\subset W$ of origin, for all initial condition $w(0)\in\bar{W}$, all the exosystems have their states exponentially synchronize on a manifold determined by $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ with $w_0\in\mathcal{W}^0$.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\alpha^*(T,t)<1$ from A4) and $\nu_{max}\le0$ from Poisson stability (by contradiction), then apply Lemma 1.

nodes.name: Linearization matrices
nodes.statement: Before proceeding the main results, some matrices are firstly introduced, arising from the linearization of nonlinear dynamics on the equilibrium of origin. \begin{equation} A_i = \left[ \frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_i}\right]_{x_i=0}, \quad B_i = g_i(0), \quad \quad C_i= \left[ \frac{\partial h_i }{\partial x_i}\right]_{x_i=0}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Remainder of linear approximation
nodes.statement: Denote by $\psi_{f}$ the reminder of the linear approximation of a vector function $f$, that is, \begin{equation} f(x)=f(0)+\left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right|_{x=0} x + \psi_f(x). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Jacobian matrix
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{D}f$ denote the Jacobian matrix of vector function $f$, that is, $\mathrm{D}f(x) = \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}$.

nodes.name: Vanishing of linearization remainder
nodes.statement: It follows that $\lim_{x\rightarrow 0}\psi_f(x)=0$ and $\lim_{x\rightarrow 0}\mathrm{D}\psi_f(x)=0$.

nodes.name: Mean Jacobian operator
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation} \mathrm{ M}f(x,h)=\left(\int^1_0 \mathrm{D}f(x+th)dt\right), \end{equation} then by mean-value theorem, \begin{equation} \psi_f(x+h)=\psi_f(x)+\mathrm{M}\psi_f(x,h)h. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: According to Assumption A2), it is true that there exists a matrix $K_i$ such that $A_i+B_iK_i$ is Hurwitz for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$. Noting that $\alpha_i(x_i,0)=K_ix_i$, condition 1a) follows directly. Below we show condition 1b). By Lemma \ref{le02}, there is a positive scalar $\beta_1$ such that \begin{equation} \|\delta w_i(t)\| \le \epsilon_0 e^{-\beta_1t}\|\delta w_i(0)\|, \quad \forall\,\, i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} for some positive scalar $\epsilon_0$. Consider the vector $e_{xi}=x_i-\pi_i(w_0)$. With \eqref{III09a}, its dynamics has the form \begin{equation} \dot{e}_{xi}=f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)-f_i(\pi_i(w_0))-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0). \end{equation} Making use of linear approximation and mean value theorem, one has, \begin{equation} f_i(x_i)-f_i(\pi_i(w_0))=A_ie_{xi}+\psi_{f_i}(x_i)-\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0)) = A_ie_{xi}+\mathrm{M}\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0),e_{x_i})e_{x_i} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \begin{split} g_i(x_i)&\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0) = g_i(x_i)c_i(w_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0)+g_i(x_i)K_ie_{xi}\\ =&(g_i(x_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0)))c_i(w_0)+g_i(x_i)(\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta{w_i})\delta{w_i}+K_ie_{xi})\\ =&B_iK_ie_{xi}+ \left[\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(0,x_i)x_i,\cdots, \mathrm{M}g_{im_i}(0,x_i)x_i\right]K_ie_{xi}+ g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta{w_i})\delta{w_i} \\& +\left(\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} c_{ij}(w_0)\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(\pi_i(w_0),e_{xi})\right)e_{xi} \end{split} \end{equation} where $g_{ij}(x_i)$ denotes the $j$th column vector of matrix function $g_i(x_i)$ and $c_{ij}(w_0)$ denotes the $j$th element of $c_i(w_0)$. With the above two equations, equation \eqref{III12} can be rewritten as \begin{equation} \dot{e}_{xi}=(A_i+B_iK_i)e_{xi}+ N(w_0,x_i)e_{xi}+g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta w_i)\delta w_i, \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} where \begin{equation} \begin{split} N(w_0,x_i)&=\mathrm{M}\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0),x_i-\pi_i(w_0))+\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} c_{ij}(w_0)\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(\pi_i(w_0),x_i-\pi_i(w_0)) \\&+ \left[\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(0,x_i)x_i,\cdots, \mathrm{M}g_{im_i}(0,x_i)x_i\right]K_i \end{split}. \end{equation} Since $A_i+B_iK_i$ is Hurwitz, there are a symmetric positive definite matrix $P_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i\times n_i}$ and a positive scalara $\epsilon_1$ such that \begin{equation} P_i(A_i+B_iK_i)+(A_i+B_iK_i)^TP_i+2\epsilon_1P_i<-I_{n_i}. \end{equation} By assumption A1) and noticing that condition 1a) holds, there exist sufficiently small $w_i(0)$ and $x_i(0)$ (notice that $w_0$ depends on $w_i$, $i\in\mathcal{V}$), such that the trajectories of $x_i(t)$ and $w_i(t)$ of the closed-loop system \eqref{II05} satisfy \begin{equation} \|N(w_0(t),x_i(t))\|\le \frac{1}{2\lambda_M(P_i)},\,\, \,\, \|g_i(x_i(t))\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0(t),\delta w_i(t))\|\le \frac{1}{\lambda_M(P_i)}, \quad \forall t>0. \end{equation} where $\lambda_M(P_i)$ denotes the maximum eigenvalue of $P_i$. Then consider the Lyapunov function $V_i=e_{xi}^TP_ie_{xi}$, whose derivative satisfies \begin{equation} \dot{V}_i\le - 2\epsilon_1e_{xi}^TP_ie_{xi} + 2e_{xi}^TP_i g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta w_i)\delta w_i \le -2\epsilon_1 V_i + 2\epsilon_2 \sqrt{V_i}\|\delta w_i\|, \end{equation} where $\epsilon_2>\frac{1}{\sqrt{\lambda_{m}(P_i)}}$ is a constant scalar and $\lambda_m(P_i)$ denoting the minimal eigenvalue of $P_i$. Define $\bar{V}_i=\sqrt{V}_i$, then $\bar{V}_i\ge0$ and \begin{equation} \dot{\bar{V}}_i\le -\epsilon_1\bar{V}_i+\epsilon_2 \|\delta w_i\|, \end{equation} which is equivalent to $\left(e^{\epsilon_1t}\bar{V}_i\right)'\le \epsilon_2 e^{\epsilon_1t}\|\delta w_i\|$. With \eqref{III11}, one further obtains \begin{equation} \bar{V}_i(t)\le e^{-\epsilon_1 t}\left(\bar{V}_i(0)-\frac{\epsilon_2\epsilon_0\|\delta w_i(0)\|}{\epsilon_1-\beta_1} \right) + e^{-\beta_1 t}\frac{\epsilon_2\epsilon_0\|\delta w_i(0)\|}{\epsilon_1-\beta_1}, \end{equation} from which, $\bar{V}_i(t)\rightarrow 0$ as $t\rightarrow \infty$, and so does $e_{xi}$. Using \eqref{III09b}, it can be further concluded that condition 1b) will be satisfied.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Necessity is clear. Below we show the sufficiency by using a constructive method. Assumption A2) and A3) mean that there are matrices $K_i$ and $L_i$ such that \setcounter{equation}{21} \begin{equation} A_i+B_iK_i \quad \mbox{and}\quad A_i+L_iC_i \end{equation} are Hurwitz. By them, the following matrix \begin{equation} \begin{bmatrix} A_i & B_iK_i \\ -L_iC_i & A_i+B_iK_i+L_iC_i \end{bmatrix} \end{equation} is also Hurwitz. Suppose there are two maps $\pi_i(w_0)$ and $c_i(w_0)$ satisfying \eqref{III09}, then set the dynamic controller to be \begin{subequations} \begin{align} &u_i=\alpha_i(z_i,w_i)=c_i(w_i)+K_i(z_i-\pi_i(w_i)), \\ &\dot{z}_{i}=\eta_i(z_i,h_i)=f_i(z_{i})+g_i(z_{i})u_i+L_i(h_i(z_i)-h_i(x_i)), \end{align} \end{subequations} for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$. Define the augmented state $\tilde{x}_i = [x_i^T, z_i^T]^T$, and maps \begin{gather} \tilde{f}_i({\tilde{x}_i})=\begin{bmatrix} f_i(x_i)\\ -L_ih_i(x_i)+L_ih_i(z_i)+f_i(z_i) \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)=\begin{bmatrix} g_i(x_i) \\ g_i(z_i) \end{bmatrix}, \nonumber \\ \tilde{\pi}_i(w_0)=\begin{bmatrix} \pi_i(w_0) \\ \pi_i(w_0) \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{h}_i(\tilde{x}_i)=h_i(x_i). \end{gather} With them, one has \begin{equation} \dot{\tilde{x}}_i = \tilde{f}_i(\tilde{x}_i)+\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)u_i, \quad \tilde{y}_i=\tilde{h}_i(\tilde{x}_i), \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\frac{\partial \tilde{\pi}_i}{\partial w_0} s(w_0) = \tilde{f}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))+\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))c_i(w_0), \\ &\tilde{h}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))+q(w_0)=0. \end{split} \end{equation} The Jacobian matrices of $\tilde{f}_i(\tilde{x}_i)$ and $\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)$ have the form of \begin{equation} \tilde{A}_i=\left[ \frac{\partial \tilde{f}_i}{\partial \tilde{x}_i} \right]_{\tilde{x}_i=0}=\begin{bmatrix} A_i & 0 \\ -L_iC_i & A_i+L_iC_i \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{B}_i=\left[ \frac{\partial \tilde{g}_i}{\partial \tilde{x}_i} \right]_{\tilde{x}_i=0}=\begin{bmatrix} B_i & 0 \\ 0 & B_i \end{bmatrix} \end{equation} Noting that $\tilde{A}_i+\tilde{B}_i[0, K_i]$ has exactly the form \eqref{III23} and that controller \eqref{III24a} can be rewritten as $u_i=c_i(w_i)+[0, K_i](\tilde{x}_i-\tilde{\pi}_i(w_i))$, by Lemma \ref{le03} conditions 1a) and 1b) are satisfied for multi-agent system \eqref{III26} with controller \eqref{III24a}, and subsequently conditions 2a) and 2b) are satisfied for the closed-loop system \eqref{II07}. Therefore the output feedback synchronized regulator problem is solved under controller \eqref{III24}.

nodes.statement: For the sack of simpleness, a multi-agent system of three nodes is taken as an illustrated example. These nodes are described respectively by the following equations. \begin{figure} \centering \includegraphics[width=0.8\textwidth]{graphs.pdf}\\ \caption{Three kinds of graphs involved in the communication of agents} \end{figure} \begin{itemize} \item Agent-1 is with state $x_1\in\mathbb{R}$, and $\dot{x}_1=x_1^2+u_1$ and $y_1=x_1$. \item Agent-2 is with state $x_2\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\dot{x}_{21}= -x_{21}+x_{22}, \quad \dot{x}_{22}=x_{21}^2+u_{22},\\ &y_{2}=x_{21} \end{split} \end{equation} \item Agent-3 with state $x_3\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\dot{x}_{31}=x_{32},\quad \dot{x}_{32}=-x_{31}+x_{32} - x_{31}^3+u_3 \\ & y_3 = x_{31} \end{split} \end{equation} \end{itemize} The dynamics that their outputs want to manifest is a sinusoid wave, formulated by \begin{equation} \dot{w}_0=s(w_0)=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & \tau\\ -\tau & 0 \end{bmatrix}w_0, \quad q(w_0)=w_{01} \end{equation} where $\tau$ denotes the angle frequency of the sinusoid wave. It can be seen after transition time, all the agents have their outputs not only synchronize but also demonstrate a sinusoid wave, although the associated communication graph is randomly switching.

nodes.statement: &\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)\\ &y_i+q(w_0)\rightarrow 0.

nodes.statement: \dot{x}_i = f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(x_i,0), \quad i\in\mathcal{V}

nodes.name: Regulator equations
nodes.statement: &\frac{\partial \pi_i}{\partial w_0} s(w_0) = f_i(\pi_i(w_0))+g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0) \\ &h_i(\pi_i(w_0))+q(w_0)=0
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: State feedback regulator
nodes.statement: u_i = \alpha_i(x_i,w_i)=c_i(w_i)+K_i(x_i-\pi_i(w_i)), \quad i\in\mathcal{V}.
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.label: III10

nodes.name: Exponential decay of synchronization error
nodes.statement: \|\delta w_i(t)\| \le \epsilon_0 e^{-\beta_1t}\|\delta w_i(0)\|, \quad \forall\,\, i\in\mathcal{V},

nodes.name: Error dynamics
nodes.statement: \dot{e}_{xi}=f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)-f_i(\pi_i(w_0))-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0).
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.label: III12

nodes.name: Linearization of f_i difference
nodes.statement: f_i(x_i)-f_i(\pi_i(w_0))=A_ie_{xi}+\psi_{f_i}(x_i)-\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0)) = A_ie_{xi}+\mathrm{M}\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0),e_{x_i})e_{x_i}
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Expansion of input term
nodes.statement: \begin{split} g_i(x_i)&\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0) = g_i(x_i)c_i(w_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0)+g_i(x_i)K_ie_{xi}\\ =&(g_i(x_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0)))c_i(w_0)+g_i(x_i)(\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta{w_i})\delta{w_i}+K_ie_{xi})\\ =&B_iK_ie_{xi}+ \left[\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(0,x_i)x_i,\cdots, \mathrm{M}g_{im_i}(0,x_i)x_i\right]K_ie_{xi}+ g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta{w_i})\delta{w_i} \\& +\left(\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} c_{ij}(w_0)\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(\pi_i(w_0),e_{xi})\right)e_{xi} \end{split}
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Rewritten error dynamics
nodes.statement: \dot{e}_{xi}=(A_i+B_iK_i)e_{xi}+ N(w_0,x_i)e_{xi}+g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta w_i)\delta w_i, \quad i\in\mathcal{V},
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Nonlinear term N
nodes.statement: \begin{split} N(w_0,x_i)&=\mathrm{M}\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0),x_i-\pi_i(w_0))+\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} c_{ij}(w_0)\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(\pi_i(w_0),x_i-\pi_i(w_0)) \\&+ \left[\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(0,x_i)x_i,\cdots, \mathrm{M}g_{im_i}(0,x_i)x_i\right]K_i \end{split}.
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Lyapunov inequality
nodes.statement: P_i(A_i+B_iK_i)+(A_i+B_iK_i)^TP_i+2\epsilon_1P_i<-I_{n_i}.
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.label: III17

nodes.name: Smallness bounds
nodes.statement: \|N(w_0(t),x_i(t))\|\le \frac{1}{2\lambda_M(P_i)},\,\, \,\, \|g_i(x_i(t))\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0(t),\delta w_i(t))\|\le \frac{1}{\lambda_M(P_i)}, \quad \forall t>0.
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Lyapunov derivative bound
nodes.statement: \dot{V}_i\le - 2\epsilon_1e_{xi}^TP_ie_{xi} + 2e_{xi}^TP_i g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta w_i)\delta w_i \le -2\epsilon_1 V_i + 2\epsilon_2 \sqrt{V_i}\|\delta w_i\|,
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Bound on sqrt V
nodes.statement: \dot{\bar{V}}_i\le -\epsilon_1\bar{V}_i+\epsilon_2 \|\delta w_i\|,
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Comparison bound
nodes.statement: \bar{V}_i(t)\le e^{-\epsilon_1 t}\left(\bar{V}_i(0)-\frac{\epsilon_2\epsilon_0\|\delta w_i(0)\|}{\epsilon_1-\beta_1} \right) + e^{-\beta_1 t}\frac{\epsilon_2\epsilon_0\|\delta w_i(0)\|}{\epsilon_1-\beta_1},
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Hurwitz matrices
nodes.statement: A_i+B_iK_i \quad \mbox{and}\quad A_i+L_iC_i

nodes.name: Closed-loop observer matrix
nodes.statement: \begin{bmatrix} A_i & B_iK_i \\ -L_iC_i & A_i+B_iK_i+L_iC_i \end{bmatrix}
nodes.section: 3.3 Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.label: III23

nodes.name: Observer-based controller
nodes.statement: &u_i=\alpha_i(z_i,w_i)=c_i(w_i)+K_i(z_i-\pi_i(w_i)), \\ &\dot{z}_{i}=\eta_i(z_i,h_i)=f_i(z_{i})+g_i(z_{i})u_i+L_i(h_i(z_i)-h_i(x_i)),
nodes.section: 3.3 Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.label: III24a

nodes.name: Augmented maps
nodes.statement: \tilde{f}_i({\tilde{x}_i})=\begin{bmatrix} f_i(x_i)\\ -L_ih_i(x_i)+L_ih_i(z_i)+f_i(z_i) \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)=\begin{bmatrix} g_i(x_i) \\ g_i(z_i) \end{bmatrix}, \nonumber \\ \tilde{\pi}_i(w_0)=\begin{bmatrix} \pi_i(w_0) \\ \pi_i(w_0) \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{h}_i(\tilde{x}_i)=h_i(x_i).
nodes.section: 3.3 Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.label: III25

nodes.name: Augmented system
nodes.statement: \dot{\tilde{x}}_i = \tilde{f}_i(\tilde{x}_i)+\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)u_i, \quad \tilde{y}_i=\tilde{h}_i(\tilde{x}_i), \quad i\in\mathcal{V},
nodes.section: 3.3 Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.label: III26

nodes.name: Augmented regulator equations
nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\frac{\partial \tilde{\pi}_i}{\partial w_0} s(w_0) = \tilde{f}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))+\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))c_i(w_0), \\ &\tilde{h}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))+q(w_0)=0. \end{split}
nodes.section: 3.3 Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.label: III27

nodes.name: Augmented Jacobians
nodes.statement: \tilde{A}_i=\left[ \frac{\partial \tilde{f}_i}{\partial \tilde{x}_i} \right]_{\tilde{x}_i=0}=\begin{bmatrix} A_i & 0 \\ -L_iC_i & A_i+L_iC_i \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{B}_i=\left[ \frac{\partial \tilde{g}_i}{\partial \tilde{x}_i} \right]_{\tilde{x}_i=0}=\begin{bmatrix} B_i & 0 \\ 0 & B_i \end{bmatrix}
nodes.section: 3.3 Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Leader-following coupled exosystem
nodes.statement: \dot{w}_i=s(w_i)+\sum_{j=0}^N \bar{a}_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i), \quad i\in\mathcal{V},

nodes.name: Leader-following controller
nodes.statement: \left\{ \begin{split} \dot{w}_i& =s(w_i)+\sum_{j=0}^N \bar{a}_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i))\\ \dot{z}_i& = \eta_i(z_i,y_i)\\ u_i &= \alpha_i(z_i,w_i) \end{split}, \right. \quad i\in\mathcal{V}

nodes.name: Leader-following regulation
nodes.statement: \lim_{t\rightarrow 0} \left(h_i(x_i)+q(w_0)\right)\rightarrow 0,

nodes.name: Sinusoid exosystem
nodes.statement: \dot{w}_0=s(w_0)=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & \tau\\ -\tau & 0 \end{bmatrix}w_0, \quad q(w_0)=w_{01}

nodes.name: Bound the consensus rate $\alpha^*(T,t)<1$ from A4)
nodes.statement: According to Assumption A4) and definition \eqref{III03}, it follows that transition matrix $\Phi(t+(k-1)T,t+kT)$ is stochastic, indecomposable and aperiodic, and has exactly one trivial eigenvalue $1$ associated with eigenvector $\mathbf{b}$. Therefore, $\alpha^*(T,t)<1$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the consensus rate $\alpha^*(T,t)<1$ from A4)

nodes.name: Show $\nu_{max}\le0$ by contradiction with Poisson stability
nodes.statement: On the other hand, with assumption A1), $\nu_{max}\le 0$. If not, for any given $\epsilon$, there is a time $T_\epsilon$, such that for any $0<\|\delta w^0\|<\epsilon$, $\|\Phi_t^s(w^0+\delta w^0)\|>\epsilon$ for all $t>T_\epsilon$. This is contradictory to the feature of Poisson stable \cite{IsidoriTAC1990}.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\nu_{max}\le0$ by contradiction with Poisson stability

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 1 to conclude exponential synchronization
nodes.statement: With $\nu_{max}\le0$ and $\alpha^*(T,t)<1$, making use of Lemma \ref{le01} yields that there is a neighborhood $\bar{W}\subset W$ of origin, for all initial condition $w(0)\in\bar{W}$, all the exosystems have their states exponentially synchronize on a manifold determined by $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ with $w_0\in\mathcal{W}^0$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 1 to conclude exponential synchronization

nodes.name: Choose Hurwitz gain $K_i$ by A2)
nodes.statement: According to Assumption A2), it is true that there exists a matrix $K_i$ such that $A_i+B_iK_i$ is Hurwitz for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$. Noting that $\alpha_i(x_i,0)=K_ix_i$, condition 1a) follows directly.
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Choose Hurwitz gain $K_i$ by A2); condition 1a) follows

nodes.name: Announce proof of condition 1b)
nodes.statement: Below we show condition 1b).
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Announce proof of condition 1b)

nodes.name: Exponential decay of $\delta w_i$ by Lemma 2
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{le02}, there is a positive scalar $\beta_1$ such that \begin{equation} \|\delta w_i(t)\| \le \epsilon_0 e^{-\beta_1t}\|\delta w_i(0)\|, \quad \forall\,\, i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} for some positive scalar $\epsilon_0$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Exponential decay of $\delta w_i$ by Lemma 2

nodes.name: Introduce error $e_{xi}$ and its dynamics
nodes.statement: Consider the vector $e_{xi}=x_i-\pi_i(w_0)$. With \eqref{III09a}, its dynamics has the form \begin{equation} \dot{e}_{xi}=f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)-f_i(\pi_i(w_0))-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Introduce error $e_{xi}$ and its dynamics

nodes.name: Expand the nonlinear terms by linearization and mean-value t
nodes.statement: Making use of linear approximation and mean value theorem, one has, \begin{equation} f_i(x_i)-f_i(\pi_i(w_0))=A_ie_{xi}+\psi_{f_i}(x_i)-\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0)) = A_ie_{xi}+\mathrm{M}\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0),e_{x_i})e_{x_i} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \begin{split} g_i(x_i)&\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0) = g_i(x_i)c_i(w_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0)+g_i(x_i)K_ie_{xi}\\ =&(g_i(x_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0)))c_i(w_0)+g_i(x_i)(\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta{w_i})\delta{w_i}+K_ie_{xi})\\ =&B_iK_ie_{xi}+ \left[\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(0,x_i)x_i,\cdots, \mathrm{M}g_{im_i}(0,x_i)x_i\right]K_ie_{xi}+ g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta{w_i})\delta{w_i} \\& +\left(\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} c_{ij}(w_0)\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(\pi_i(w_0),e_{xi})\right)e_{xi} \end{split} \end{equation} where $g_{ij}(x_i)$ denotes the $j$th column vector of matrix function $g_i(x_i)$ and $c_{ij}(w_0)$ denotes the $j$th element of $c_i(w_0)$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Expand the nonlinear terms by linearization and mean-value theorem

nodes.name: Rewrite error dynamics as Hurwitz part plus perturbations
nodes.statement: With the above two equations, equation \eqref{III12} can be rewritten as \begin{equation} \dot{e}_{xi}=(A_i+B_iK_i)e_{xi}+ N(w_0,x_i)e_{xi}+g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta w_i)\delta w_i, \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite error dynamics as Hurwitz part plus perturbations

nodes.name: Lyapunov matrix $P_i$ from Hurwitz property
nodes.statement: Since $A_i+B_iK_i$ is Hurwitz, there are a symmetric positive definite matrix $P_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i\times n_i}$ and a positive scalara $\epsilon_1$ such that \begin{equation} P_i(A_i+B_iK_i)+(A_i+B_iK_i)^TP_i+2\epsilon_1P_i<-I_{n_i}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Lyapunov matrix $P_i$ from Hurwitz property

nodes.name: Smallness of perturbation terms for small initial conditions
nodes.statement: By assumption A1) and noticing that condition 1a) holds, there exist sufficiently small $w_i(0)$ and $x_i(0)$ (notice that $w_0$ depends on $w_i$, $i\in\mathcal{V}$), such that the trajectories of $x_i(t)$ and $w_i(t)$ of the closed-loop system \eqref{II05} satisfy \begin{equation} \|N(w_0(t),x_i(t))\|\le \frac{1}{2\lambda_M(P_i)},\,\, \,\, \|g_i(x_i(t))\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0(t),\delta w_i(t))\|\le \frac{1}{\lambda_M(P_i)}, \quad \forall t>0. \end{equation} where $\lambda_M(P_i)$ denotes the maximum eigenvalue of $P_i$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Smallness of perturbation terms for small initial conditions

nodes.name: Bound derivative of Lyapunov function $V_i$
nodes.statement: Then consider the Lyapunov function $V_i=e_{xi}^TP_ie_{xi}$, whose derivative satisfies \begin{equation} \dot{V}_i\le - 2\epsilon_1e_{xi}^TP_ie_{xi} + 2e_{xi}^TP_i g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta w_i)\delta w_i \le -2\epsilon_1 V_i + 2\epsilon_2 \sqrt{V_i}\|\delta w_i\|, \end{equation} where $\epsilon_2>\frac{1}{\sqrt{\lambda_{m}(P_i)}}$ is a constant scalar and $\lambda_m(P_i)$ denoting the minimal eigenvalue of $P_i$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Bound derivative of Lyapunov function $V_i$

nodes.name: Differential inequality for $\sqrt{V_i}$
nodes.statement: Define $\bar{V}_i=\sqrt{V}_i$, then $\bar{V}_i\ge0$ and \begin{equation} \dot{\bar{V}}_i\le -\epsilon_1\bar{V}_i+\epsilon_2 \|\delta w_i\|, \end{equation} which is equivalent to $\left(e^{\epsilon_1t}\bar{V}_i\right)'\le \epsilon_2 e^{\epsilon_1t}\|\delta w_i\|$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Differential inequality for $\sqrt{V_i}$

nodes.name: Comparison bound gives $e_{xi}\to0$
nodes.statement: With \eqref{III11}, one further obtains \begin{equation} \bar{V}_i(t)\le e^{-\epsilon_1 t}\left(\bar{V}_i(0)-\frac{\epsilon_2\epsilon_0\|\delta w_i(0)\|}{\epsilon_1-\beta_1} \right) + e^{-\beta_1 t}\frac{\epsilon_2\epsilon_0\|\delta w_i(0)\|}{\epsilon_1-\beta_1}, \end{equation} from which, $\bar{V}_i(t)\rightarrow 0$ as $t\rightarrow \infty$, and so does $e_{xi}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Comparison bound gives $e_{xi}\to0$

nodes.name: Conclude condition 1b) via (III09b)
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{III09b}, it can be further concluded that condition 1b) will be satisfied.
nodes.section: 3.2 Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Conclude condition 1b) via (III09b)

nodes.name: Necessity clear
nodes.statement: Necessity is clear. Below we show the sufficiency by using a constructive method.
nodes.section: 3.3 Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Necessity clear; sufficiency by construction

nodes.name: Hurwitz gains $K_i$, $L_i$ from A2), A3)
nodes.statement: Assumption A2) and A3) mean that there are matrices $K_i$ and $L_i$ such that \setcounter{equation}{21} \begin{equation} A_i+B_iK_i \quad \mbox{and}\quad A_i+L_iC_i \end{equation} are Hurwitz.
nodes.section: 3.3 Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Hurwitz gains $K_i$, $L_i$ from A2), A3)

nodes.name: Closed-loop observer matrix is Hurwitz
nodes.statement: By them, the following matrix \begin{equation} \begin{bmatrix} A_i & B_iK_i \\ -L_iC_i & A_i+B_iK_i+L_iC_i \end{bmatrix} \end{equation} is also Hurwitz.
nodes.section: 3.3 Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Closed-loop observer matrix is Hurwitz

nodes.name: Define the observer-based dynamic controller
nodes.statement: Suppose there are two maps $\pi_i(w_0)$ and $c_i(w_0)$ satisfying \eqref{III09}, then set the dynamic controller to be \begin{subequations} \begin{align} &u_i=\alpha_i(z_i,w_i)=c_i(w_i)+K_i(z_i-\pi_i(w_i)), \\ &\dot{z}_{i}=\eta_i(z_i,h_i)=f_i(z_{i})+g_i(z_{i})u_i+L_i(h_i(z_i)-h_i(x_i)), \end{align} \end{subequations} for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$.
nodes.section: 3.3 Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem
nodes.statement_short: Define the observer-based dynamic controller

nodes.name: Define augmented state and maps
nodes.statement: Define the augmented state $\tilde{x}_i = [x_i^T, z_i^T]^T$, and maps \begin{gather} \tilde{f}_i({\tilde{x}_i})=\begin{bmatrix} f_i(x_i)\\ -L_ih_i(x_i)+L_ih_i(z_i)+f_i(z_i) \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)=\begin{bmatrix} g_i(x_i) \\ g_i(z_i) \end{bmatrix}, \nonumber \\ \tilde{\pi}_i(w_0)=\begin{bmatrix} \pi_i(w_0) \\ \pi_i(w_0) \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{h}_i(\tilde{x}_i)=h_i(x_i). \end{gather}
nodes.section: 3.3 Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.statement: With them, one has \begin{equation} \dot{\tilde{x}}_i = \tilde{f}_i(\tilde{x}_i)+\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)u_i, \quad \tilde{y}_i=\tilde{h}_i(\tilde{x}_i), \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\frac{\partial \tilde{\pi}_i}{\partial w_0} s(w_0) = \tilde{f}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))+\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))c_i(w_0), \\ &\tilde{h}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))+q(w_0)=0. \end{split} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Compute augmented Jacobians
nodes.statement: The Jacobian matrices of $\tilde{f}_i(\tilde{x}_i)$ and $\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)$ have the form of \begin{equation} \tilde{A}_i=\left[ \frac{\partial \tilde{f}_i}{\partial \tilde{x}_i} \right]_{\tilde{x}_i=0}=\begin{bmatrix} A_i & 0 \\ -L_iC_i & A_i+L_iC_i \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{B}_i=\left[ \frac{\partial \tilde{g}_i}{\partial \tilde{x}_i} \right]_{\tilde{x}_i=0}=\begin{bmatrix} B_i & 0 \\ 0 & B_i \end{bmatrix} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 3 to the augmented system
nodes.statement: Noting that $\tilde{A}_i+\tilde{B}_i[0, K_i]$ has exactly the form \eqref{III23} and that controller \eqref{III24a} can be rewritten as $u_i=c_i(w_i)+[0, K_i](\tilde{x}_i-\tilde{\pi}_i(w_i))$, by Lemma \ref{le03} conditions 1a) and 1b) are satisfied for multi-agent system \eqref{III26} with controller \eqref{III24a}, and subsequently conditions 2a) and 2b) are satisfied for the closed-loop system \eqref{II07}.
